topicTitle: Introduction, Maternity Cycle, Antenatal, Intranatal, and Postnatal Care
anchorText: MATERNITY CYCLE AND PERIODS OF GROWTH
alt: Five-phase maternity cycle from fertilization through antenatal, intranatal, postnatal, and inter-conceptional periods
caption: Maternity cycle: fertilization in the tubal ampulla, antenatal (prenatal) period, intranatal period, postnatal period, then the inter-conceptional interval. Implantation in the endometrium occurs 8 to 10 days after fertilization.

topicTitle: Immunization, Cold Chain, National Immunization Schedule, and AEFI
anchorText: COLD CHAIN HIERARCHY AND VULNERABILITIES IN INDIA
alt: Indian vaccine cold chain from state WIC/WIF through district and PHC ILRs to sub-centre vaccine carriers
caption: Cold chain in India: state WIC/WIF holds 3 months of stock; district and PHC ILR/DF hold 1 month; sub-centre vaccine carriers last 24 to 48 hours. Failure risk is highest at session sites.

topicTitle: Analytical Epidemiology: Case Control, Cohort, Cross-Sectional, and Ecological Studies
anchorText: DIFFERENCES BETWEEN CASE-CONTROL AND COHORT STUDIES
alt: Case-control studies look backward from disease to exposure; cohort studies look forward from exposure to disease
caption: Case-control studies start with diseased and non-diseased people and look backward to exposure; they give an odds ratio. Cohort studies start with exposed and unexposed people who are disease-free and follow them forward; they give incidence and relative risk.
prompt: Create a square 1:1 medical textbook infographic titled "Case-control versus cohort". Do not draw any empty box, frame, placeholder square, border, watermark, or logo in any corner. Fill the whole square canvas with the diagram. Title at top-left. Clean white background, navy and teal two-panel flowchart, large readable sans-serif labels, no watermark, no logo. Left panel Case-control: start with Cases and Controls, arrow backward to Exposure, output Odds Ratio, good for rare disease. Right panel Cohort: start with Exposed and Unexposed, arrow forward to Disease, output Relative Risk, good for rare exposure. Perfect square.

topicTitle: Infectious Disease Epidemiology, Transmission Dynamics, and Disease Control
anchorText: CLASSIFICATION OF MODES OF DISEASE TRANSMISSION
alt: Direct and indirect modes of disease transmission including contact, droplet, inoculation, soil, vertical, and vehicle routes
caption: Modes of transmission. Direct: physical contact, droplet spray under 1 metre, inoculation, contact with soil, and vertical (transplacental) spread. Indirect routes include vehicles such as the classic environmental 5 Fs.

anchorText: Lead Time and Associated Methodological Biases
alt: Screening timeline from biological onset through first detectable point, lead time, critical point, clinical diagnosis, and death
caption: Lead time is the interval from detection by screening to the usual clinical diagnosis. Screening helps only between the first detectable point and the final critical point. Lead-time bias lengthens apparent survival without delaying death.
